title: Pause physics command queue during physics processing
body:
Fixes #109554.

> [!WARNING]
> This change is a bit crude and will likely be a performance regression for some projects that rely on the `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread` project setting, but I'm not sure how else to fix this race condition, other than to somehow introduce synchronization between `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT`, `PhysicsDirectSpaceState*D` and `PhysicsDirectBodyState*D`, which has its own complications/downsides.

What this does is make it so that `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT::sync` and `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT::end_sync` (called [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8aa37cab8950351d96f541581abdc42136283f24/main/main.cpp#L4738) and [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8aa37cab8950351d96f541581abdc42136283f24/main/main.cpp#L4777) in the main loop) actually "pauses" and "unpauses" the asynchronous processing of commands in the command queue of `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT`, thereby ~~effectively disabling `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread` during the physics processing part of the main loop~~.

EDIT: It's probably more fair to say that we are _deferring_ `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread` with this change now, since we're still offloading non-read/non-sync tasks to the physics thread, but until after the physics processing is done.

This would mean that we resolve the (apparently long-standing) race conditions between `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT::_thread_loop` and `PhysicsDirectSpaceState*D` (and `PhysicsDirectBodyState*D` as well) while preserving the ability for users to freely perform physics queries in parallel as much as they want[^1] from any thread[^2] when `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread` is enabled.

Note however that much of the benefit from `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread` comes from doing the actual physics step asynchronously, which would still be the case, as that happens after `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT::end_sync`.

[^1]: Only as long as it's done during physics processing, but this is already being enforced [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8aa37cab8950351d96f541581abdc42136283f24/modules/godot_physics_3d/godot_physics_server_3d.cpp#L194), albeit not very rigorously.
[^2]: You're technically only allowed to fetch `PhysicsDirectSpaceState*D` from the main thread, as seen [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8aa37cab8950351d96f541581abdc42136283f24/servers/physics_server_3d_wrap_mt.h#L115), but there's nothing stopping you from caching the instance and using it from multiple threads, which should be fine for that class specifically, since physics queries should (at least in theory) all be read-only.
